pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
DEPTH PERCEPTION

Sandbox Software, Pittsburgh. 3:00 in the morning.

The render of the century is crawling down the monitor one scan line at a time: the box art for Depth Perception, a perfect checkerboard running to the horizon, chrome spheres, a glass cube, a red teapot and the morning sun coming up behind them all. It has been rendering for eleven hours. It is 99% done. Everybody went home. Doc Leo, our lighting director, left his spotlight on.

Then COUNT POLYGON crept in through the modem.

The Count lives on polygons. He took the gold sphere's and left it an icosahedron. He took the teapot's and left it a brick. He spread his henchmen through every scene of the render: wireframes that were never finished, jaggies made of nothing but stair steps, and polygon bats.

He missed one. RAY, the chrome sphere from every ray tracing demo ever made, still has every polygon he was born with. Roll him through six scenes, collect the red, green and blue lenses, and get him to each scene's vanishing point, where all the parallel lines meet. The box art goes to the printer at nine.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type DEPTH and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster plays the music and the digitized sound effects; without one, the PC speaker beeps along. Every picture in the game was rendered ahead of time, so a 386 plays it as well as a 486.

From the menu, pick Play. Leave the menu alone for half a minute to watch a demonstration. Read Storyline shows how the night went wrong; Read Instructions is a short version of this manual.

Light and lives

Ray runs on light. He starts with 100 and three lives. Henchmen, steam and bats cost light; light bulbs, friends and THE CHEZ's charge port give it back. Fall into the void and the render of Ray simply falls apart: you start that scene over, with every lens you have found still in your pocket. Press F2 to see your score, light and lives.

pages.head: Controls
pages.html:
Controls

↑ ↓ ← →
or W S A D		Roll. Ray stops when you let go - he's a very well-behaved sphere.
Q E
keypad 7 9 1 3		Roll diagonally: Q up-left, E up-right; the number pad corners go all four ways.
SpaceFire a ray of light the way you last rolled. It renders a wireframe into a crystal (touch the crystal for points) and takes faces off Count Polygon.
F1-F6Help, status, music on/off, sound on/off, save, load.
EscQuit to the menu.

A joystick works too: push to roll, button 1 fires.

pages.head: Pulling Focus
pages.html:
Pulling Focus

Every scene in the render has two planes: the near plane and the far plane. A camera can only focus on one at a time, and in Depth Perception that is the whole trick:

Sharp things are solid. A blur isn't there.

Near blocks are amber; far blocks are cyan. When the near plane is in focus, amber blocks are crisp and solid and cyan ones are soft, see-through blurs you can roll right through. Pull focus to the far plane and it's the other way round.

Focus rings

Roll onto a focus ring (a chrome ring set in the floor) to pull focus to the other plane. The lens inside the ring glows the color of where it will take you. Ray's own bands tell you which plane is in focus: amber near, cyan far.

Glass walkways

Glass walkways are only there in their own plane: an amber walkway holds you up when the near plane is in focus and is just a blur over the void when it isn't. Violet auto-focus panels drift in and out of focus on their own; wait for them to sharpen, then roll. A panel flickers pink twice just before it blurs out, so a flicker means stay put.

A fresh render

Pulling focus re-renders the scene the way it was: photons and bulbs come back, and gates close again. The lenses you've found stay with you.

pages.head: Things in the Render
pages.html:
Things in the Render

PhotonA little star of light: 25 points.
Light bulb30 light in the first two scenes, 20 in the next two and 15 in the last two: the closer the render is to done, the scarcer light gets.
Red, green and blue lensesOne of each in every scene. The RGB gate before the vanishing point takes one of each.
RGB gateThree glass doors in a row: red, green, blue. Each opens only for its lens.
Vanishing pointThe white light at the end of each scene.
SlopesGolden chevrons in the Fractal Peaks pull you the way they point. Ride them down; don't ride them into a pit.
TeapotsThe Utah teapot, the most rendered object there is. In the Teapot Temple they puff steam at you.
THE CHEZA 1976 1/2 CitiCar, plugged in on the rear passenger side. Push against its charge port for light.

pages.head: Friends and Fiends
pages.html:
Friends and Fiends

Friends

Teddy, a Pembroke Welsh corgi with one ear taller than the other, strolls the Checkerboard. Gwinn, sitting pretty in her pink collar, keeps the Glass Garden. Doc Leo, our lighting director (fedora, green tie, red sneakers and a rubber chicken on a leash), paces the Teapot Temple. Bump into any of them for a little light. Henchmen that bump into them get rendered.

Fiends

WireframesNever finished. One ray renders them into crystals.
JaggiesAliasing with teeth. They hop along their beat.
Your dark doubleThe Hall of Mirrors' reflection that rolls at you when you get close.
SteamFrom the teapots. Hot.
Polygon batsThe Count's, from their nests at the vanishing point.
ShardsThrown by the four prisms in Count Polygon's arena. A prism glows pink just before it throws. Shards are slow and a ray shatters them.
COUNT POLYGONTwenty faces of vampire. He swoops round you and dives. A ray cracks him, a second shatters him, a third takes faces off: twenty, then eight. When the eight are gone he coughs up the blue lens he swallowed and flees into the far plane, where he waits with four faces, then a triangle, then a point. What he leaves behind opens the last door.

pages.head: The Six Scenes
pages.html:
The Six Scenes

1. The Checkerboard. Where every render begins. Learn to pull focus.

2. The Glass Garden. Crystals, glass tiles and auto-focus panels over the void.

3. The Hall of Mirrors. Nine rooms joined by near doors and far doors, around a middle room drawn isometrically, as if the camera had swung round to a corner. Which one of you is real?

4. Fractal Peaks. Infinitely detailed, mostly downhill. The plateau at the top is seen isometrically, amber blocks standing a tier taller than cyan.

5. Teapot Temple. A colonnade, three shrines, an isometric sanctum around the vanishing point and a parked CitiCar.

6. The Vanishing Point. Where all parallel lines meet, and Count Polygon waits in an arena drawn isometrically: amber near cubes stand a full tier tall, cyan far cubes half that. Beat him in the near plane, then follow him up through the blue gate into the far plane.

pages.head: Tips from the Render Farm
pages.html:
Tips from the Render Farm

  • Look before you roll: if a block is soft and see-through, it isn't there right now.
  • A focus ring always drops you off on its far side. Step back onto it to pull focus back.
  • A lens boxed in by blocks of one color is a puzzle, not a wall: find the ring that turns that color to a blur.
  • Fire before a wireframe reaches you: a rendered crystal is worth points; a bump costs light.
  • The auto-focus panels keep time. Count it while you wait on solid ground.
  • Lost a life? The scene starts over, but your lenses don't.
  • Count Polygon doesn't move until you come within reach. Pick your spot first, and keep a cube between you and the prisms.
  • He swoops to one side, then the other, then dives. Line up as he swings by, and roll clear when he dives.
  • Not every mirror in the Hall of Mirrors is a wall.

pages.head: How to Register
pages.html:
This is shareware!

You may copy Depth Perception and give it to your friends, upload it to your favorite BBS, and play it as long as you like. If you enjoy it, please register for $15.

Registered players get:

  • Depth Perception II: Bump Map on a 3 1/2" disk
  • The Depth Perception Hint Book
  • A pair of red and blue cardboard glasses you will not need
  • Our thanks, and Doc Leo's

Send a check or money order for $15, payable to Sandbox Software, to:

Sandbox Software
Dept. DEPTH
P.O. Box 000
Pittsburgh, PA 15213

Please allow 4 to 6 weeks for delivery, or about one overnight render.
